claims.head: A shadow job for Hagel, Cirelli and Holmberg
claims.call: The Lightning’s L2 (Hagel, Cirelli and Holmberg) spends at least 46% of its 5-on-5 time against the Red Wings’ first line, against about 32% with no line matching.
claims.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Hagel’s line (Hagel, Cirelli and Holmberg) out against opponents’ first lines, far more often than chance would suggest. notes.text: Marco Kasper is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 14 games.
Dylan Larkin is suspended and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-six forward.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 70% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 22 seconds at a time, against 70 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (23 of 30 changes).

stakes: The Red Wings go in tied for seventh in the Atlantic with 17 points, a point behind the Lightning, tied for fourth. A regulation win for the Red Wings would lift them past the Lightning. The Lightning have two games in hand.

DET.head: The Red Wings have a hill to climb
DET.body: Detroit is on the second night of a back-to-back, while Tampa Bay has been out-chancing opponents lately and has home-ice advantage. The Red Wings’ best way through is a power play that gets going.

story.head: The Red Wings played last night
paras: The Red Wings (7-5-3) beat Florida 5-3 last night, while the Lightning (8-3-2) lost 5-4 in a shootout to Nashville on Saturday. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Red Wings last (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Bolts fourth (tied for ninth). The Atlantic has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Red Wings have played better than their record (.567) says: their chances are worth about .617, and their finishing has held them back. The Lightning’s record (.692) is about what their chances are worth.

The Red Wings draw more penalties than they take (2nd), but ice the puck a lot (30th). The Lightning, by contrast, rarely ice the puck (3rd). The Red Wings also block more shots than almost anyone (2nd), so the Red Wings are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Lightning’s shots. The Lightning get into more chippy games than almost anyone (2nd) and let the point shots come and guard the net (4th). The Lightning’s defensemen shoot a lot, and the Red Wings’ not so much.

Alex DeBrincat (7 G / 9 A / 16 P in 15 GP) leads the Red Wings in scoring. Viktor Arvidsson (8 G / 7 A / 15 P in 15 GP) has a team-high eight goals, with seven points in his last five games. For the Lightning, Nikita Kucherov (4 G / 14 A / 18 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Brandon Hagel (8 G / 8 A / 16 P in 13 GP) has a team-high eight goals.
John Gibson (4-5-1 / .860 SV% in 10 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Detroit, but is expected to start. Andrei Vasilevskiy (6-3-1 / .877 SV% in 10 GS) is expected to go for Tampa Bay.
At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Hagel, Cirelli and Holmberg out against the other team’s top line, so watch for them against DeBrincat, Finnie and Arvidsson.
